fixes.explanation: Joppa doesn't show up anywhere in this passage, friend. The crowd gets into the boats and goes to Capernaum (John 6:24). Good try, and now you know the town the verse names.
That's exactly what Jesus says. He tells them, "…you ate the loaves and had your fill." He doesn't even answer the when question. He goes straight to the why.
Walking on the sea isn't what Jesus brings up here. What He names is the loaves: "…you ate the loaves and had your fill." He goes right to it.

Eternal is the word. Jesus says to work for "…food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you." A cookie on my counter lasts maybe a week if I hide it from myself. Jesus is talking about food that endures to eternal life.
That's it. Jesus says, "The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent." They asked about works, plural, and He gives them one. I think that's a lot simpler than I'd have guessed.

That's a thoughtful guess, but Jesus doesn't go there. He answers, "The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent." The crowd asked what to do, and He points them to believing. One work, and I'd still have been hunting for a checklist.

Giving is a good thing, but Jesus doesn't name it here. He says, "The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent." The crowd asked what work to do, and He gives them one work. I'd have bet on a longer answer, friend.
Manna. The crowd says, "Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness…" They bring it up right after asking, "What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You?" (John 6:30).

Right. Moses, Israel's leader, is not the giver here. Jesus says, "…it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven." The giver is the Father, and the bread He gives is the true bread from heaven.

Reward is a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't say it here. He says He will lose none of those the Father gave Him, "…but raise them up at the last day." The verse is about Him raising them up. That's the part I'd hold onto.

That's what they say. "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?" They bring up His father and mother as part of their question. I think that's a hard thing to hear about someone whose family you know.

Teaching is a good thought, but Jesus doesn't use that word here. He says, "And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh." He says He gives it for the life of the world. That's the part I keep turning over.

His word is a good guess, but Jesus doesn't name it here. He says, "And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh." He names His flesh. He says He will give it for the life of the world.

That's what He says. "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you." The Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). He opens with "Truly, truly," like He did earlier in this passage.

Signs aren't what Jesus talks about in this verse, friend. He says, "…unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you." The Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). Those are heavy words, and Jesus says them straight.
Synagogue. John 6:59 says, "Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum." So that's where He was teaching when He said this. I like to picture the people in the back leaning in.
